Maria: Heads up — Finance just approved the new tier migration for Standard->Premium next month. We need a quick capacity plan for the expected burst from quota increases.
Alex: How big is the expected uplift? any numbers from PM/finance?
Maria: PM sent projections: ~45% more concurrent requests from mid-tier customers during weekdays, translating to ~28k additional GPU hours/month if we keep current batching. (source: finance deck)
Deepa: 28k is doable if we reassign some reserved slots, but region distribution matters — 70% of the extra traffic is expected in eu-west1 and us-west2.
Ravi: eu-west1 is already tight. Current spare GPU hours there are ~3.2k/month after commitments. We'd be ~10k short just in eu-west1.
Jordan: If we can't add hardware in time, we should consider a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap + queued bursts. Rate-limited tails are better than 500s.
Maria: Agreed. Ops asks for a formal request to cloud infra by EOD: numbers per region, timeline, and fallback. I'll draft.
Alex: Draft should include two alternative mitigations: 1) increase reserved capacity (buy extra pods/GPU pool) 2) apply tiered concurrency limits + soft queuing with 429s and Retry-After header.
Deepa: Also add smart routing: route mid-tier traffic to cheaper model variants (quantized) where latency sensitivity is low — reduces GPU hours by ~22% in internal sims.
Ravi: Quick note on procurement lead times: GPU procurement for dedicated is ~6-8 weeks for physical; cloud-spot/commit adjustments can be done in 48-72 hours but cost delta ~+18%.
Jordan: Can we leverage burst pool in us-central as a cross-region fallthrough? Network egress might add 20-80ms but better than errors.
Maria: Yes include burst pool plan and cost delta. OpsBot: [autoscaler] new capacity request created: req-67321 — pending approvals (link: https://redwood.ops/reqs/67321).
Alex: For the request, I recommend asking for staged capacity: Week1 +20% GPU hours, Week2 +35%, Week3 full +45% — gives time to validate traffic and avoid big upfront cost.
Deepa: Add a canary window where we bump quotas for 5% of customers and monitor tail latencies/evictions for 72h. If KV cache pressure increases, the quantized fallback should be enabled automatically.
Ravi: Monitoring checklist: GPU util, queue length, OOMs, model latency p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, network egress. Need alert thresholds.
Jordan: I'll add alerts: p95 > 850ms for >5m, queue length > 500, GPU util > 92% for >10m -> auto-scale attempt.
Maria: Cost note for Finance: worst-case cloud commit + burst pool = estimated +$120k/month. Soft-limits + throttling path = estimated +$12k/month operational cost (more developer time).
Alex: Decision tradeoff: pay for reserved to keep SLAs vs throttle and accept some UX degradation. Recommend hybrid: reserve for eu-west1 and us-west2; throttle in other regions.
Deepa: Action items: Maria to send request to procurement + infra (with regional numbers). Ravi to scope hardware lead times and cloud commit options. Jordan to prepare alert runbook and canary plan. Alex to write rollback + comms draft for Support.
Maria: I'll assemble the packet and post to #eng-infra later today. If anyone has model-level sims (batching impact, quantization gains) DM me before 16:30. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ravi: DM'd Alex the eu-west1 utilization CSV and a quick script to simulate tenant spike.
Alex: Pushed a sim snippet to the thread:```python
# rough sim: extra_gpu_hours = base_hours * (1 + uplift) / batching_gain
base_hours = 64000
uplift = 0.45
batching_gain = 1.18
print(int(base_hours * (1+uplift) / batching_gain))
```
Jordan: OpsBot: created a temporary dashboard: "tier-migration-forecast" (link: https://dash.redwood/tier-migration-forecast).
Maria: Thanks all. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10am to lock the request. :checkered_flag:
